To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) IL-10 gene-modified DC can inhibit EAM, and (2) this inhibition is mediated via downregulation of IL-1beta expression and upregulation of IL10 and TGF-beta expression in the myocardium.

IL-10-modified iDC can induce tolerance of EAM in vivo, which is related to its ability to inhibit the proliferation and differentiation of CD4+ T cells, and to promote the differentiation and function of Treg cells, thus inhibiting the inflammatory reaction in the heart.

the iDC transfected with pcDNA3-IL10 gene could inhibit the development of EAM in rats, which might be related to the down-regulation of IL-1b, IL-2, IL-6, TNF-a, IFN-g and IL-17A, and the up-regulation of TGF-b and IL-10.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of DCs transfected with IL-10 gene on experimental autoimmune myocarditis.
the effect of IL-10 modified DC on the treatment of EAM and its possible mechanism.
the effect of iDCs modified with pcDNA3-IL10 on EAM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

IL-10 gene-modified dendritic cells can effectively prevent the progression of experimental autoimmune myocarditis and the underlying mechanisms may be related to the down-regulation of inflammatory response, the reduction in the number of infiltrating CD4+ T lymphocytes and the increase in the number of regulatory CD4+ CD25+ Foxp3+ Treg cells.

the IL-10 gene modified dendritic cells can effectively inhibit the development of autoimmune myocarditis in mice, which may be related to the down-regulation of inflammatory factors, the increase of regulatory T cells and the decrease of Th17 cells.

the results of the present study demonstrated the therapeutic effect of IL-10 gene-modified DC in EAM, and this effect was related to the inhibition of the Th17 cells and Th17-related inflammatory response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IL-10 gene modified dendritic cells could be a new strategy for the treatment of autoimmune myocarditis and the mechanism of this therapy is the induction of antigen-specific tolerance.

IL-10 gene modified DCs can induce antigen-specific tolerance in EAM mice, which may be associated with the inhibition of Th1 and Th2 responses, the enhancement of regulatory T cell responses, and the down-regulation of the expression of MHC class II and costimulatory molecules.
we have successfully established an experimental autoimmune myocarditis (EAM) rat model by using the immunization of cardiac myosin peptide (CSP) and complete Freund’s adjuvant (CFA).
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-10 transgenic iDCs can be used as a potential therapeutic strategy for the treatment of autoimmune myocarditis.
the IL-10 gene modified DC can be used to induce antigen-specific tolerance, and it can be used for treatment of immune-inflammatory myocardial injury.
DC transfection with IL-10 gene can induce immune tolerance and protect mice against EAM.
